turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: I came in because I keep getting these nagging thoughts that I forgot something important. Like maybe I left my aunt’s medicine out wrong, or didn’t set up materials in my classroom safely. Even when I’m pretty sure I handled it, the doubt just keeps coming back.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient describes recurrent nagging doubts about having forgotten important safety-related tasks despite being fairly sure they were handled.

turns.doctor_question: When those doubts pop up, do you feel driven to repeatedly check or redo things to make sure everything is okay?
turns.patient_response: Yes. Before I leave home or my classroom, I’ll check the same things a few times—the pill organizer, the stove, my lesson plans. Sometimes I just replay in my head what I did. I keep doing it until I feel calm enough to leave, even though it can make me late.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient describes repeatedly checking the pill organizer, stove, and lesson plans and mentally replaying actions until calm, causing lateness.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from these doubts about checking and safety, do you find yourself constantly worrying about many other everyday areas of your life, like finances, health, or your family?
turns.patient_response: I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed myself worrying about lots of different things like that all the time.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient says they have not noticed themselves worrying about many different everyday areas all the time.
